domain_models.TITLE: Event-data validity
domain_models.STATE_AND_OBJECTS: Let W denote in-scope work occurrences, R recorded observations, X an extraction transformation, and L the resulting event representation. Recording is a potentially incomplete, many-to-many correspondence ρ⊆W×R: an occurrence may have no matched record, and an administrative record may have no matched in-scope occurrence. X acts on the record collection to produce L and may select, join, correlate and abstract. Neither correspondence nor transformation is assumed invertible; recorded timestamps may differ from occurrence times.
domain_models.INFERENCE_AND_LIMITS: A result computed on L is a claim about W only through justified recording and extraction assumptions. Exact identity of L and reproducibility of X do not validate the correspondence ρ. Adequacy is relative to a declared question Q, target unit U and window T; a defect matters when it changes the claim required by Q.
domain_models.OPERATING_ACCOUNT: Investigate event classes and source examples, reconcile material transformations and population boundaries, then preserve the remaining uncertainty in the chosen analysis. A surprising result can return directly to source interpretation. Correction, narrowing and non-use are legitimate branches, not failed completion of a pipeline.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_FAILURE: A status transition is logged on form submission at the end of a shift: a sequence miner faithfully orders records but the interpreted work chronology is false. Correct schema and checksums do not cure this.
domain_models.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_FORM: One bounded question, a tested event dictionary or small semantic sample, a reproducible query and explicit exclusions. Rich quality metrics are triggered by heterogeneity or consequential defects.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.EVENT_SEMANTICS_AND_SOURCE_PROVENANCE: Primary concern: distinguish a recording act from the work it denotes; retain source identity sufficient for material trace-back.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CASE_OR_OBJECT_NOTION: Declare the case, encounter, object or decision unit before assessing event counts; a row identifier is not automatically the analytical unit.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTRACTION_ABSTRACTION_AND_ORDERING: Record joins, filters, lifecycle interpretation, abstraction and ordering; preserve ambiguity where the sources do not justify one order.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.LOG_COMPLETENESS_NOISE_AND_SELECTION: Assess missingness, duplicate records, selection and noise against the actual question; neither perfect-log demands nor convenient-extract acceptance is justified.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.MODEL_CLASS_AND_DISCOVERY_ASSUMPTIONS: Discovery is downstream and optional. No choice of miner repairs an unjustified event-to-work interpretation by itself.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.REFERENCE_MODEL_AND_CONFORMANCE_SEMANTIC: If conformance is performed, map the event vocabulary to the reference explicitly; schema validity is not conformity to the intended process.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.FITNESS_PRECISION_GENERALISATION_AND_SIM: Model quality scores are not log-validity measures. Input validity is assessed before and alongside downstream quality evaluation.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.TEMPORAL_VALIDITY_AND_DRIFT: Version recording and extraction practices; changed instrumentation can invalidate apparently stable event semantics.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PREDICTION_CAUSALITY_AND_INTERVENTION_BO: Correctly extracted observations can support description without identifying causal effects. Prediction additionally requires decision-time availability.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.HUMAN_VALIDATION_PRIVACY_AND_DECISION_CO: Use relevant source custodians and participants to test meanings; collect and retain only the detail justified by a legitimate consumer.

domain_models.TITLE: Case/object semantics
domain_models.STATE_AND_OBJECTS: Represent events E, objects O, object types τ and participation R⊆E×O. A case-centric projection πc maps events to traces under case notion c; one event may participate in several objects. Attributes and object relationships can change over time, which must be represented when consequential.
domain_models.INFERENCE_AND_LIMITS: Projection changes the represented relation. Two case notions may yield different frequencies and directly-follows edges without any change in E or W. Object-centric representations preserve selected relations but do not remove identity or abstraction assumptions. Type-level and identifier-aware nets have different guarantee domains.
domain_models.OPERATING_ACCOUNT: Select the relation needed by the question; test convergence/divergence and shared-event duplication; use an object-aware representation only when it retains a consequential relation. For executable models, name the exact formalism and establish its supported soundness properties. Revisit the representation when interpretation cost or uncertainty dominates its gain.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_FAILURE: An invoice shared by two orders becomes two copied events in a flattened order log. Counting those copies as two invoice executions is a representational error, not discovered rework.
domain_models.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_FORM: A case log with an explicit chosen identifier and a small cardinality check. A typed event–object table is the next step when interactions matter; an executable object-centric net is a further, separately justified choice.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.EVENT_SEMANTICS_AND_SOURCE_PROVENANCE: Events retain identity across object participation; an event copied into several traces is not automatically several real occurrences.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CASE_OR_OBJECT_NOTION: Central: choose case notion or typed object relations according to the question; distinguish object types, identifiers and changing relationships.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTRACTION_ABSTRACTION_AND_ORDERING: Record flattening, correlation and abstraction rules and their effects on ordering and counts. Ambiguous identity is not solved by serialization.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.LOG_COMPLETENESS_NOISE_AND_SELECTION: Completeness must be assessed for both events and relationships; missing object links can distort synchronisation and duration even with complete activity labels.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.MODEL_CLASS_AND_DISCOVERY_ASSUMPTIONS: Use the exact case/object formalism and supported constructs; OCPNs, type-level workflow nets and identifier-aware trees are not interchangeable guarantees.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.REFERENCE_MODEL_AND_CONFORMANCE_SEMANTIC: Reference semantics must match the object/identity model. Ordinary trace conformance cannot automatically certify interaction behaviour.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.FITNESS_PRECISION_GENERALISATION_AND_SIM: Additional representational detail is not universal superiority. Evaluate task adequacy, behavioural quality and human/computation cost separately.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.TEMPORAL_VALIDITY_AND_DRIFT: Preserve identity and relation changes over time; a stable label does not prove a stable object relationship.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PREDICTION_CAUSALITY_AND_INTERVENTION_BO: Object context may improve a predictor or diagnostic but does not identify intervention effects or grant action authority.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.HUMAN_VALIDATION_PRIVACY_AND_DECISION_CO: Validate identity conventions and relation meaning with custodians and consumers; rich links can increase re-identification and interpretation burden.

domain_models.TITLE: Discovery and identifiability
domain_models.STATE_AND_OBJECTS: A discovery procedure Dθ maps an event representation L to a model M in a chosen class C. θ includes thresholds, objective, noise handling and implementation settings. The observed log is a finite sample; the model language ℒ(M) can contain unobserved behaviours.
domain_models.INFERENCE_AND_LIMITS: A construction guarantee such as soundness is a property of M under its formal semantics. Rediscovery additionally assumes a compatible generating class and adequate observations. Neither entails unique reconstruction of the organisational mechanism. Different algorithms expose different structures and biases: procedural, declarative, region-based, evolutionary, abstract or local.
domain_models.OPERATING_ACCOUNT: Choose representation and purpose, disclose bias, compare adequate alternatives and investigate material exceptions. Domain knowledge can guide the search if its provenance is visible. Use local views without global claims where sufficient. Revise or withhold a structural inference when alternate models cannot be discriminated.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_FAILURE: The finite traces ab and ba support both a concurrent two-task mechanism and an exclusive choice between two sequential branches. Log agreement alone cannot identify which internal mechanism produced them.
domain_models.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_FORM: A labelled directly-follows relation or one explicit constraint can answer a narrow question. Executable discovery is triggered by a need to reason about allowed behaviour, execution or richer conformance.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.EVENT_SEMANTICS_AND_SOURCE_PROVENANCE: Discovery assumes an event vocabulary whose activity meanings have been established; it does not discover those meanings from labels alone.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CASE_OR_OBJECT_NOTION: Case-centric traces or object participation determine the basic input relation and therefore the recoverable structure.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTRACTION_ABSTRACTION_AND_ORDERING: Abstraction, total-order choices and filtering are part of the inductive bias; retain their effect on the discovered model.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.LOG_COMPLETENESS_NOISE_AND_SELECTION: Noise and incomplete sampling alter observed order relations; infrequent does not mean invalid, and absent does not mean impossible.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.MODEL_CLASS_AND_DISCOVERY_ASSUMPTIONS: Central: disclose model class, algorithm, objective, parameters and scoped guarantees; preserve guarded alternatives rather than selecting a universal winner.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.REFERENCE_MODEL_AND_CONFORMANCE_SEMANTIC: A discovered model is descriptive unless separately authorised. Using it as a reference does not make its inferred constraints obligations.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.FITNESS_PRECISION_GENERALISATION_AND_SIM: Evaluate fitness, precision, generalisation and simplicity separately and with applicable measures; a miner’s objective is not a complete validation.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.TEMPORAL_VALIDITY_AND_DRIFT: A discovered model describes a dated observation regime; changed behaviour or logging can invalidate its previous scope.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PREDICTION_CAUSALITY_AND_INTERVENTION_BO: Recovered control flow is not automatically causal structure. A model useful for replay need not be adequate for intervention prediction.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.HUMAN_VALIDATION_PRIVACY_AND_DECISION_CO: Participants test interpretation and useful abstraction; richer discovery is warranted only when a consumer can use its distinctions.

domain_models.TITLE: Conformance and authority
domain_models.STATE_AND_OBJECTS: Conformance relates a log L, reference M, mapping a, semantics s and, where used, costs c. Alignments minimise a defined cost over allowed model/log moves; token replay counts token discrepancies under its own replay semantics. An uncertain log U may denote a set of admitted realisations.
domain_models.INFERENCE_AND_LIMITS: The result establishes a relation under (M,a,s,c), not an all-purpose verdict. Minimum cost is not the true causal history. For uncertain data, a minimum and maximum over U bound only the declared set of possibilities, not a probability. Normative force depends on the origin and authority of M, not on the optimiser.
domain_models.OPERATING_ACCOUNT: Establish reference provenance, choose the least costly adequate comparison, expose approximation and interpret mismatch through rival data/model/execution/exception causes. A confirmed problem branches to data correction, model repair, process change or authorised rule revision. Preserve unresolved explanations when evidence cannot discriminate.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_FAILURE: A mandatory manual check occurs but is never logged. The observed trace deviates from the reference, yet the alignment alone cannot distinguish omitted recording from omitted work.
domain_models.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_FORM: One explicitly interpreted rule and a traceable event check. Token replay, exact alignments, multi-perspective constraints and uncertainty bounds are richer alternatives selected by diagnostic need.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.EVENT_SEMANTICS_AND_SOURCE_PROVENANCE: Event meaning and model activity mapping must agree at the relevant level; an unlogged manual activity can create apparent non-conformance.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CASE_OR_OBJECT_NOTION: The reference and log must use compatible case/object semantics; trace comparisons can miss cross-case obligations.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTRACTION_ABSTRACTION_AND_ORDERING: Ordering and abstraction determine which moves are compared; conversion must not silently turn uncertain order into certain violation.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.LOG_COMPLETENESS_NOISE_AND_SELECTION: Missing, duplicate or selected events are rival explanations for mismatch; log defects and process defects are not the same conclusion.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.MODEL_CLASS_AND_DISCOVERY_ASSUMPTIONS: Discovery is optional: the reference can be supplied independently. Formalisms define the behaviours and constraints the checker can compare.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.REFERENCE_MODEL_AND_CONFORMANCE_SEMANTIC: Central: identify reference origin, version, authority, move semantics, costs and approximation; comparison is not normative authorisation.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.FITNESS_PRECISION_GENERALISATION_AND_SIM: Fitness measures observed correspondence; precision and other dimensions answer different questions and cannot be inferred from an optimal alignment.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.TEMPORAL_VALIDITY_AND_DRIFT: Version reference expectations and observation windows; a changed descriptive model must not silently amend an obligation.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PREDICTION_CAUSALITY_AND_INTERVENTION_BO: A deviation suggests diagnostic questions, not a causal remedy. Changing a process or rule requires separate evidence and authority.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.HUMAN_VALIDATION_PRIVACY_AND_DECISION_CO: Communicate alternative explanations to relevant participants and reference owners; people-related allegations need contestable, bounded evidence.

domain_models.TITLE: Model evaluation
domain_models.STATE_AND_OBJECTS: Let Q(M,L,P,T,u) denote a vector of claim-specific evaluations under population P, time T and consumer task u, not a universal scalar. Fitness concerns observed behaviour admitted; precision concerns excess permitted behaviour under a definition; generalisation concerns unseen valid behaviour; simplicity concerns usable representation/cost.
domain_models.INFERENCE_AND_LIMITS: No component logically entails all others. A model with ℒ(M)=Σ* has perfect language-inclusion fitness for every L while admitting arbitrary sequences. Measure definitions and representation choices affect comparisons. Train/test design identifies a target performance only under its sampling and dependence assumptions.
domain_models.OPERATING_ACCOUNT: State the evaluation question and units, select applicable measures and baselines, isolate test information and disclose unavailable measures. Inspect sensitivity to data quality, representation and parameter choices. A decision-specific trade-off can select a model, but it must not masquerade as a context-free ranking.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_FAILURE: A benchmark reports only successful metric computations, thereby dropping the large or difficult logs on which a method fails. The resulting average answers a selected problem, not the advertised common comparison.
domain_models.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_FORM: A few explicit behavioural tests plus a relevant complexity/usefulness check may suffice for a local question. Broad empirical comparisons require a fuller experimental design.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.EVENT_SEMANTICS_AND_SOURCE_PROVENANCE: Evaluation on a syntactically valid log still depends on event semantics; model scores do not establish what was observed.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CASE_OR_OBJECT_NOTION: Use cases, objects, prefixes or process generators as the unit appropriate to the claim; do not count dependent prefixes as independent cases.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTRACTION_ABSTRACTION_AND_ORDERING: Fix or compare abstraction, order and preprocessing fairly; differences in preparation can dominate algorithm differences.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.LOG_COMPLETENESS_NOISE_AND_SELECTION: Representativeness, noise, censoring and excluded runs change what an evaluation estimates.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.MODEL_CLASS_AND_DISCOVERY_ASSUMPTIONS: Compare algorithms within declared model and output semantics; unsupported constructs and failed conversions are material outcomes.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.REFERENCE_MODEL_AND_CONFORMANCE_SEMANTIC: Conformance-derived metrics require compatible reference semantics; descriptive model quality does not confer normative authority.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.FITNESS_PRECISION_GENERALISATION_AND_SIM: Central: separate the four questions, specify actual metrics and retain trade-offs, missing values and known formal weaknesses.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.TEMPORAL_VALIDITY_AND_DRIFT: Match temporal splits to prospective claims and keep tuning information out of the future test regime.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PREDICTION_CAUSALITY_AND_INTERVENTION_BO: Predictive scores, model quality and causal utility are different targets; none supplies the others without additional assumptions.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.HUMAN_VALIDATION_PRIVACY_AND_DECISION_CO: Consumer priorities justify local trade-offs; reproducibility and expert usability checks complement rather than replace empirical validity.

domain_models.TITLE: Performance and organisational inference
domain_models.STATE_AND_OBJECTS: Observed times define intervals between recorded lifecycle events. Resource attributes denote accounts, roles, people or systems according to source semantics. Context includes case mix, load, queues, object relations, batching, calendars and unobserved prerequisites.
domain_models.INFERENCE_AND_LIMITS: Δt between two records is an elapsed interval; active effort or waiting attribution requires additional phase and context evidence. A handoff relation constructed from a trace is an operational relation, not necessarily collaboration or influence. A diagnosed bottleneck is a hypothesis about a mechanism, not an automatically identified cause.
domain_models.OPERATING_ACCOUNT: Use timing and interaction patterns to focus inquiry, validate resource and lifecycle meanings, compare relevant contexts and consult participants. Distinguish communicated findings, agreed action, implemented action and measured outcome. Scenario analysis is conditional on a model and does not establish achieved benefit.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_FAILURE: A long interval before approval is attributed to the approver, while an unlogged prerequisite or batch-recording policy explains it. A shared account then wrongly concentrates the apparent delay on one person.
domain_models.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_FORM: A traceable elapsed-time comparison and a focused operational conversation can be enough. Queueing, object-centric timing and simulation are triggered by a consequential contextual dependency.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.EVENT_SEMANTICS_AND_SOURCE_PROVENANCE: Timestamp and resource fields must be interpreted as recording semantics, not automatically as effort or person identity.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CASE_OR_OBJECT_NOTION: Case/object relations determine which intervals and interactions belong together; shared events can distort flattened duration and rework.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTRACTION_ABSTRACTION_AND_ORDERING: Lifecycle pairing, calendars, batching and ordering are necessary for stronger duration claims; preserve omitted phases.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.LOG_COMPLETENESS_NOISE_AND_SELECTION: Censoring, incomplete cases, unlogged prerequisites and selective resource capture affect performance attribution.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.MODEL_CLASS_AND_DISCOVERY_ASSUMPTIONS: A descriptive process map may be sufficient; executable or simulation models add assumptions that need separate validation.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.REFERENCE_MODEL_AND_CONFORMANCE_SEMANTIC: Performance deviation from a target is not proof of a violated obligation or culpable worker; the reference target requires interpretation.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.FITNESS_PRECISION_GENERALISATION_AND_SIM: Fitness can support replay but cannot validate timing semantics or organisational explanations. Human interpretability is a separate requirement.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.TEMPORAL_VALIDITY_AND_DRIFT: Compare like periods and distinguish demand/case-mix changes from performance changes; dates and source regimes matter.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PREDICTION_CAUSALITY_AND_INTERVENTION_BO: Pattern, cause, feasible remedy and measured consequence are separate claims; intervention benefit requires evidence beyond delay localisation.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.HUMAN_VALIDATION_PRIVACY_AND_DECISION_CO: Operational participants validate omitted context and resource meaning; privacy, fairness and a real decision consumer constrain personal attribution.

domain_models.TITLE: Drift and temporal revision
domain_models.STATE_AND_OBJECTS: A monitored feature distribution Pt is affected by work, population, instrumentation and extraction. A detector compares windows or maintains adaptive state; it has finite memory, delay and false-alarm behaviour. A descriptive model Mt and authorised reference Rt need not change together.
domain_models.INFERENCE_AND_LIMITS: A detected distributional change does not identify which underlying component changed. A forgotten event is not disproved behaviour. Updating Mt to describe new observations does not authorise changing Rt. A stable reference can still require an explicit, legitimate revision when circumstances change.
domain_models.OPERATING_ACCOUNT: Monitor only when timely response matters; investigate alarms through rival observation/process explanations; version the data and models; choose batch or streaming according to latency and cost. Branch to model revision, instrumentation correction, process action or no change. Preserve prior reference meaning where continuity matters.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_FAILURE: A software release splits one activity label into two, causing a drift alarm. Automatically retraining the compliance standard would normalise a logging change rather than evaluate the work.
domain_models.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_FORM: A dated snapshot and periodic comparison with a known source-change log. Streaming is triggered by meaningful latency or resource constraints, not by novelty.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.EVENT_SEMANTICS_AND_SOURCE_PROVENANCE: Changes in event meaning and recording behaviour are possible drift causes and must be investigated.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CASE_OR_OBJECT_NOTION: Case or object correlation changes can alter apparent process behaviour without changing work.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTRACTION_ABSTRACTION_AND_ORDERING: Version transformations, label abstraction and arrival ordering; late events and partial traces require explicit treatment.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.LOG_COMPLETENESS_NOISE_AND_SELECTION: Sampling, noise and incomplete cases affect alarms; a stream window is not the whole historical population.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.MODEL_CLASS_AND_DISCOVERY_ASSUMPTIONS: Adaptive discovery is one response, not a mandatory consequence of every detected shift.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.REFERENCE_MODEL_AND_CONFORMANCE_SEMANTIC: Keep descriptive model revision distinct from authorised reference revision; drift does not itself amend obligations.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.FITNESS_PRECISION_GENERALISATION_AND_SIM: Evaluate detector delay, false alarms and feature sensitivity separately from model-quality scores.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.TEMPORAL_VALIDITY_AND_DRIFT: Central: define observation windows, regimes, forgetting, recurrence and revision continuity; distinguish abrupt, gradual and other material change patterns.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PREDICTION_CAUSALITY_AND_INTERVENTION_BO: Distribution shift can invalidate prediction or causal-policy evaluation; detection is not a causal explanation or action warrant.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.HUMAN_VALIDATION_PRIVACY_AND_DECISION_CO: A consumer must be able to investigate and act on alarms; excessive churn and alert burden are real costs.

domain_models.TITLE: Prediction and intervention
domain_models.STATE_AND_OBJECTS: At decision time t, It denotes available information and At feasible actions. Prediction estimates an outcome conditional on It; an intervention claim concerns outcomes under a specified action or policy. Prefixes of one case and cases sharing resources may be dependent. Calibration data and policy versions are part of the state.
domain_models.INFERENCE_AND_LIMITS: P(Y|A=a,It) need not equal an interventional outcome distribution because action selection can be confounded. Prediction-time availability is a precondition for prospective evaluation. Conformal coverage is marginal under its conditions, not individual certainty, and policy feedback can alter the distribution on which earlier evidence depended.
domain_models.OPERATING_ACCOUNT: Define the decision occasion and available features, evaluate against adequate baselines using valid splits and censoring treatment, and expose useful uncertainty. Recommendations additionally require causal identification or explicit hypothesis status, feasible authorised action and new outcome evidence. Re-evaluate after intervention changes exposure or behaviour; abstain when no useful decision can be supported.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_FAILURE: A predictor reads the final resolution code from a completed case record while claiming to predict resolution early. Removing the field may destroy its benchmark advantage; deployment has not disproved learning, but the evaluation never tested the advertised task.
domain_models.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_FORM: A transparent prediction or prioritisation rule with correct temporal inputs and a real consumer. Causal policy optimisation, calibration layers and automation each require a separate trigger and justification.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.EVENT_SEMANTICS_AND_SOURCE_PROVENANCE: Feature meanings and update times must be established; a final case attribute may not have existed at prediction time.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CASE_OR_OBJECT_NOTION: Use the correct case, prefix, object context or decision occasion; account for dependence and resource coupling.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTRACTION_ABSTRACTION_AND_ORDERING: Prevent future-derived aggregation and label leakage; preserve the state actually observable at each decision occasion.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.LOG_COMPLETENESS_NOISE_AND_SELECTION: Completed-case selection, censoring, class imbalance and support for actions affect evaluation and causal identification.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.MODEL_CLASS_AND_DISCOVERY_ASSUMPTIONS: Predictive models need not be discovered process models; their architecture and information access must be compared fairly.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.REFERENCE_MODEL_AND_CONFORMANCE_SEMANTIC: A reference process can constrain feasible actions but prediction does not validate its normative authority.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.FITNESS_PRECISION_GENERALISATION_AND_SIM: Evaluate predictive discrimination, calibration, coverage, timing, cost and decision utility for their distinct purposes; a process fitness score is not predictive utility.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.TEMPORAL_VALIDITY_AND_DRIFT: Use a split and calibration regime matching prospective use; drift and intervention feedback can invalidate earlier results.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PREDICTION_CAUSALITY_AND_INTERVENTION_BO: Central: distinguish prediction, explanation, causal identification, feasible advice, authorised action and measured effect.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.HUMAN_VALIDATION_PRIVACY_AND_DECISION_CO: Human review and abstention need an actual recipient and capacity; sensitive features, fairness and action consequences require accountable decisions.

domain_models.TITLE: Reproducibility and evidence custody
domain_models.STATE_AND_OBJECTS: An analytical result has a chain of source snapshot, extraction, transformations, model/algorithm versions, parameters, evaluation and interpretation. Evidence also has dependence across repeated logs, sites, synthetic generators and publication versions.
domain_models.INFERENCE_AND_LIMITS: Re-running the same computation establishes repeatability of a declared transformation, not the truth of its assumptions. Stable results across selected parameters do not establish semantic validity. Repeated runs and publications on one log increase analysis depth, not the number of independent organisational replications.
domain_models.OPERATING_ACCOUNT: Preserve the minimal executable and interpretive chain, allow material trace-back, challenge plausible alternatives and record failed/negative results. Use domain participation as evidence, not an oracle. Where data cannot be shared, describe the blocked claim and avoid calling a substitute experiment an exact replication.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_FAILURE: A complete script repeatedly reproduces a false personal ranking because the resource field denotes a shared service account. Computational custody makes the mistake inspectable but does not cure it.
domain_models.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_FORM: A reproducible query/script, identified data and versions, meaningful exclusions and a short interpretation note. More elaborate evidence infrastructure is justified only by scale, longevity, sensitivity or consequence.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.EVENT_SEMANTICS_AND_SOURCE_PROVENANCE: Retain source identifiers and interpretation provenance sufficient to investigate material claims without assuming byte identity proves meaning.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CASE_OR_OBJECT_NOTION: Record population and dependency units, including cases, objects, prefixes, logs and sites.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTRACTION_ABSTRACTION_AND_ORDERING: Preserve the executable transformation chain and key abstraction/order decisions; document irrecoverable steps.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.LOG_COMPLETENESS_NOISE_AND_SELECTION: Record exclusions, repaired data, failed runs and unshareable data limits so reproducibility does not hide selection.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.MODEL_CLASS_AND_DISCOVERY_ASSUMPTIONS: Record algorithm, implementation, solver, model class, parameters and randomisation where material.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.REFERENCE_MODEL_AND_CONFORMANCE_SEMANTIC: Identify reference versions and comparison settings so a conformance result can be reconstructed and interpreted.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.FITNESS_PRECISION_GENERALISATION_AND_SIM: Preserve actual metric definitions and missing results; check material sensitivity rather than report only a preferred score.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.TEMPORAL_VALIDITY_AND_DRIFT: Keep version/cut-off identity and avoid reconstructing prediction experiments with future information.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PREDICTION_CAUSALITY_AND_INTERVENTION_BO: Auditability supports checking a causal or predictive claim but does not establish its validity; transfer remains a new claim.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.HUMAN_VALIDATION_PRIVACY_AND_DECISION_CO: Reviewers and domain participants need usable evidence with lawful access; documentation without a consumer can become ceremony.

domain_models.TITLE: Responsible use and frontier boundaries
domain_models.STATE_AND_OBJECTS: The analytical setting includes participants, custodians, consumers, permissions, disclosure boundaries, model assistants and possible harms. Emerging representations and tools add hypotheses and costs as well as capabilities. Some research questions have no adequate practical evidence yet.
domain_models.INFERENCE_AND_LIMITS: Secure computation is not necessarily private output; pseudonyms are not anonymity; fluent generated text is not validated process evidence. An expressive or mathematically sound method is not necessarily externally useful. Non-use and retirement can be positive dispositions when there is no adequate or proportionate question.
domain_models.OPERATING_ACCOUNT: State purpose and threat/decision boundaries, choose only the necessary data and methods, check generated or inferred content and provide contestability where people are affected. Evaluate current work by exact version and access level. Keep researched transfer questions unresolved instead of forcing universal adoption.
domain_models.DISCRIMINATING_FAILURE: A federated protocol hides raw logs but reveals identifying trace lengths; an LLM extracts an event absent from the narrative; a dashboard triggers sanctions without a defensible reference. Each is a different failure requiring a different check.
domain_models.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_FORM: A bounded, non-identifying analysis or an alternative non-mining method. Federation, LLM assistance, rich object identity and new collection require demonstrable value and independently checked constraints.

DOMAIN_PROFILE.EVENT_SEMANTICS_AND_SOURCE_PROVENANCE: Text-derived or inferred events remain hypotheses until source-supported interpretation is established; generated structure is not raw observation.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.CASE_OR_OBJECT_NOTION: Rich object and resource relations can improve analysis while increasing linkage and re-identification risk.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.EXTRACTION_ABSTRACTION_AND_ORDERING: Privacy transformations and text extraction alter the evidence; retain the transformation and its analytical loss.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.LOG_COMPLETENESS_NOISE_AND_SELECTION: Selective instrumentation and privacy suppression affect population claims; more collection is not an unconditional remedy.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.MODEL_CLASS_AND_DISCOVERY_ASSUMPTIONS: Frontier methods require exact formalism and version identity; benchmarks establish bounded task results, not general autonomous competence.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.REFERENCE_MODEL_AND_CONFORMANCE_SEMANTIC: No discovered regularity or generated reference acquires normative authority solely through technical production.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.FITNESS_PRECISION_GENERALISATION_AND_SIM: Evaluate analytical utility, interpretation cost and privacy/decision risks separately; popularity and dashboard presence are not quality measures.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.TEMPORAL_VALIDITY_AND_DRIFT: Version changing assistants, protocols and object models; an older benchmark cannot certify an untested current version.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.PREDICTION_CAUSALITY_AND_INTERVENTION_BO: Emerging prescription and object-centric prediction remain bounded by causal, deployment and feedback evidence requirements.
DOMAIN_PROFILE.HUMAN_VALIDATION_PRIVACY_AND_DECISION_CO: Central: legitimate purpose, proportionate collection, explicit attacker/consumer, contestability and a feasible no-use or retirement path.
